transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
Ever since my friend was killed, I’ve had this constant mix of guilt, fear, and anger. I kept thinking it would ease with time, but it hasn’t.
Do upsetting memories of your friend’s killing keep popping into your mind when you don’t want them to?
Yes. A crosswalk signal, a truck growling by, even seeing one of those walking-tour maps—suddenly it all comes back so clearly. I see my friend stepping off the curb before I can stop the memory.
Have you been avoiding places or things that remind you of your friend’s killing?

Yes. I go out of my way not to go near that intersection. And I’ve stopped signing up for most tours or safety meetings, because the conversation always seems to come back to what happened there. I just can’t bear it.
Since your friend was killed, have you been feeling constantly on guard or easily startled?
Yes. Near traffic, I’m watching every truck, every curb, every pedestrian. It feels like it’s my responsibility to notice danger before something happens again.
Has it been more than a month since your friend was killed?
Yes. It’s been going on since my friend was killed on that walking tour—about two years and three months now.
Since your friend was killed, have you been blaming yourself for what happened?

Yes. I keep thinking if I’d chosen a different route, or pushed harder about that crossing, she might still be alive. Then I get furious all over again—at the driver, and at the town for letting it happen.
Since your friend was killed, have you felt detached or cut off from other people?
Yes. Even when I’m sitting with people I’ve known for years at the senior center, I feel apart from them—like they’re all talking on one side of a window and I’m on the other.
Since your friend was killed, have you felt unable to experience positive feelings, like happiness or love?

Yes. I used to enjoy planning my garden, quilting with the ladies, theater trips, book club—now I see those things on the calendar and just feel almost nothing. Like they belonged to someone I used to be.

The duration exceeds one month and symptoms clearly cause social/emotional impairment.
